articles.title: Marido de Juliette, Kaíque Cerveny treinou em Bauru para CrossFit | G1
articles.standfirst: Campeão sul-americano atualmente, ele encarou rotina intensa de até três treinos por dia em equipe do interior de SP antes de disputar torneio nacional em 2019, no qual foi campeão.
articles.summary: Kaíque Cerveny celebra casamento com Juliette após trajetória de superação em Bauru, onde treinava três vezes ao dia para se tornar campeão nacional de CrossFit.
articles.body:
O atleta de CrossFit Kaíque Cerveny, que se casou com a campeã do BBB 21, da TV Globo, e cantora Juliette Freire em cerimônia intimista no interior da Paraíba, morou no interior paulista e treinou em uma academia de Bauru (SP) para o Campeonato Brasileiro de 2019, torneio do qual foi campeão.

Nesta quinta-feira (29), Kaíque e Juliette celebraram a união religiosa e a festa na Capela de Nossa Senhora das Graças, localizada no Instituto Ricardo Brennand, no bairro da Várzea, na Zona Oeste do Recife (PE). No dia 30 de setembro, eles realizaram um casamento intimista com familiares , em Cabaceiras (PB).

Juliette e Kaíque no Lajedo de Pai Mateus, na Paraíba — Foto: Gabriel Diniz/Reprodução

De acordo com o treinador e profissional de educação física Douglinhas Balbino, Kaíque morou e integrou a equipe bauruense por um ano e meio, motivado pelo objetivo de disputar competições internacionais.

"Ele veio treinar com alguns atletas em Bauru, pois na época o nível era muito alto. Em pouco tempo, ele elevou muito o nível físico e estratégico — que representa mais de 50% do resultado — e, desde então, bateu asas e conquistou aquilo que tanto queria. Ele sempre abdicou de muita coisa para conquistar", destacou o treinador.

Kaique Cerveny, marido de Juliette, chegou a morar e treinar em Bauru por um ano para o Campeonato Brasileiro de CrossFit — Foto: Claudiney Oliveira/Reprodução

Balbino relatou ainda que Kaíque mantinha uma rotina de dois a três treinos diários e demonstrava disciplina e convivência próxima com os colegas de equipe.

"Ele treinava em dois períodos, as vezes dependendo do tempo da preparação, três vezes ao dia. Um misto de treinamentos, onde incluía também, natação, corrida e força. Na verdade, ele sonhava em chegar no Mundial, e por isso treinava aqui em Bauru. Sempre muito dedicado e obediente; tanto no quesito atleta quanto pessoal", completa.

Na carreira, o atleta também conquistou o título do campeonato sul-americano de CrossFit e garantiu vaga no CrossFit Games.

articles.title: David Otorbi: el sueño continúa con un blindaje de 60 millones
articles.standfirst: La joya del Valencia de 19 años amplía su contrato hasta 2031 mientras se recupera de la lesión muscular que frenó su irrupción en el primer equipo
articles.summary: La joya del Valencia de 19 años amplía su contrato hasta 2031 mientras se recupera de la lesión muscular que frenó su irrupción en el primer equipo
articles.body: David Otorbi es oficialmente desde este viernes la joya de la corona del Valencia. El extremo español de origen nigeriano, uno de los talentos con mayor proyección surgidos de Paterna, continuará vinculado al club hasta 2031. La renovación la firmó el martes y el Valencia lo hizo oficial este 30 de octubre. Braulio Vázquez, nuevo director deportivo, no quiso esperar a que cumpla los diez partidos oficiales con el primer equipo que figuraban en su contrato para activar la renovación automática que le mejora el contrato ostensiblemente y le duplicará la cláusula de 30 a 60 millones de euros. De este modo, el Valencia espanta a los clubes de la Premier que ya habían ido a espiar al jugador, como hizo el Newcastle en Santander. Y de camino, reconforta al futbolista que estará lesionado cerca de dos meses tras una rotura muscular en los isquiotibiales, sufrida en el último partido de Liga en Mestalla. El veloz jugador ya estaba apareciendo de manera recurrente en los partidos del Valencia, de titular y suplente, y marcó su primer gol ante el Racing, aunque ahora tendrá que esperar para recuperarse bien. David Otorbi Ejededawe (2007), español de padres nigerianos -Monday y Patience-, se crio en el valenciano barrio de Nazaret y llegó a la cantera del Valencia en 2019, con 12 años. Mediocentro reconvertido a extremo es el jugador más joven en debutar con el Valencia en partido oficial (con 16 años, dos meses y 19 días en Copa ante el Cartagena) y también el más precoz en hacerlo en Liga (con 16 años y 306 días, frente al Barcelona). Fue Nacho Gallart, su primer entrenador en el Malva-Rosa, el que redactó el informe que proponía su ingreso en la Academia del Valencia. Pero, antes se las había hecho pasar canutas durante su etapa en el Atlético Cabanyal, otra escuela de los Poblados Marítimos fundada por el propio Gallart: "El primer año decidí no tenerlo en el equipo porque me parecía excesivamente individualista y medio lo castigué", explicaba en Radio MARCA Valencia. Fue el propio Otorbi el que pidió cambiar el equipo de Gallart, que había sido campeón esta temporada: "Yo creo que pensó: 'uf, este equipo me gusta y quiero estar y tengo que ser más asociativo y jugar más para el equipo". A partir de ese momento, encadenaron varios campeonatos hasta que llegó el Valencia y Gallart decidió convertirse en su agente. El Valencia ha cuidado del futbolista y de la persona. Lo matriculó en el colegio privado que hay junto a la ciudad deportiva de Paterna y con el que tiene un convenio de formación. Todos los días lo recogía un empleado del club para llevarlo desde su casa hasta el centro educativo y, después, a entrenarse y estudiar en la residencia de la cantera. Fue ahí donde sus compañeros -hizo buena amistad con otro canterano Leslie Okai- popularizaron el apodo de 'Pantera' por la velocidad y la fuerza de un futbolista que conoce sus propias limitaciones y cómo pulirlas: "No me gusta nada defender", confesaba hace unos meses tras su anterior renovación, "pero con los técnicos he visto mis partidos y me han ayudado a mejorar esa faceta". Seguro que le vendrá muy bien todo lo que ha aprendido del equipo de Gestión de Talento de la Academia porque tras terminar la ESO y el BTEC (FP británica) ahora se está preparando para sacarse el carné de entrenador (ahora está en el nivel 1). Este será el cuarto contrato, si se toma como tal su incorporación con 12 años, que firma David Otorbi con el Valencia. Tras fichar en 2019, renovó en octubre de 2023, en lo que fue su primer contrato profesional cuando cumplió 16 años. Como su progresión no paraba y más aún, tras debutar con el primer equipo, firmó un nuevo contrato en abril de 2026 que extendía su vínculo hasta 2028 con 30 millones de cláusula. Ahí aparecía la cláusula de renovación automática que activará el Valencia para ampliar el vínculo laboral hasta 2031 con 60 millones de cláusula.

articles.title: Las notas de la semana: Mbappé tiene que estar alucinando
articles.standfirst: Del 10 al 0, por Juan Ignacio García-Ochoa
articles.summary: Del 10 al 0, por Juan Ignacio García-Ochoa
articles.body: Mbappé se levantó el martes tan tranquilo tras la gala del Balón de Oro y se encontró con una crisis sin precedentes con China por unas palabras ¡de abril!. Lo más curioso es que en el podcast en el que habló, The Bridge, declaró que se sentía más cómodo en ese formato que con los periodistas para no meterse en líos con los titulares. ¡Pues menos mal! De todas maneras, el francés tiene que estar alucinando. "Me hace gracia el meme que hacen con ese dictador chino, es el que más uso con mis amigos", fueron las 'explosivas' declaraciones (nótese la ironía) del francés, perseguido por los líos más absurdos que se recuerdan. Aunque este ha dejado pequeño al de la bici... Con más crítica que halago por normal general, el portugués merece todo el reconocimiento por su planteamiento en el Camp Nou y por la manera en la que poco a poco está construyendo un Real Madrid competitivo. Ver a un club de barrio como el Sporting de Hortaleza jugando contra el Sevilla engrandece la Copa. Fútbol de verdad. Solo faltó que el equipo sevillano hubiera pisado Monovar. Sobresaliente también a la RFEF por aplazar la jornada del miércoles. Balón de Oro más que merecido para los dos. El delantero inglés se lo lleva tras una temporada en la que marcó 73 goles, cifra que solo superó una vez en toda la historia Leo Messi. Alexia Putellas se ha levantado como pocos esperaban de sus lesiones y vuelve a reinar en el planeta fútbol. Walter Tavares continúa haciendo historia en el baloncesto europeo. El pívot del Real Madrid alcanzó los 825 rebotes ofensivos en la Euroliga, superando el registro de Kyle Hines y convirtiéndose en el nuevo referente histórico de la competición en esta estadística. Lo hizo, además, en una contundente victoria madridista ante Baskonia (86-104). El italiano se impuso en la carrera del pasado fin de semana y el domingo lo más normal es que se convierta en el campeón más joven de la historia. Antonelli ha arrasado esta temporada y va a devolver el título a Italia 73 años después. Lo único malo es que dejará el Mundial finiquitado con cuatro carreras de antelación. Conviene darle una vuelta a esto. El pésimo inicio de temporada del Espanyol, eliminación de Copa incluida, se ha llevado por delante a Manolo González. Estaba cantado y la decisión la entiende hasta el propio técnico. Ahora llega Eder Sarabia, una garantía de buen fútbol que va a llegar como un huracán. Veremos si el cambio de rumbo funciona. La gala tuvo suspense, pero también mucho retraso y decisiones extrañas y poco comprensibles como la de que Michael Owen entregara el Balón de Oro a Alexia Putellas. ¿No había otro más apropiado? Muy desafortunadas sus declaraciones tras la derrota ante el Lugano, a lo que hay que sumar el 4-0 ante el Athletic. Tiempos complicados para el Getafe. Sancionado con dos partidos por taparse la boca durante una discusión en un partido en Brasil Que sea él quien no conozca la Ley Vinicius... Hace mucho que no está a lo que tiene que estar. Desde nuestro punto de vista, resulta surrealista la que se ha liado por las declaraciones de Mbappé. Un comentario sin mala intención ¡del mes de abril! que ha abierto una crisis sin precedentes. Curioso también que Mbappé dijera en aquella entrevista en el podcast de The Bridge que prefería antes ese formato que a los periodistas para no meterse en líos con los titulares. ¡Menos mal! El energúmeno que agredió a Camavinga tras el segundo gol del Madrid con el palo de una bandera ha sido identificado y denunciado por los Mossos. Ojalá se le aplique la máxima pena, que asciende según la Ley del Deporte a los 60.000 euros. El castigo debe ser ejemplar y, desde luego, que este personaje no vuelva a entrar a un campo de fútbol. Basta ya de cafres en el fútbol, en muchos casos amparados por los clubes. l

articles.title: Diomande en la tierra de Gento
articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Con ánimos renovados tras su victoria en el Spotify, el Madrid visita en este turno al Racing de Santander, equipo al que le une un firme parentesco histórico. En las cinco Copas de Europa de tacada del equipo de Di Stéfano, cuatro jugadores fueron titulares fijos durante todo el ciclo: el propio Di Stéfano, el vizcaíno Zárraga y dos cántabros, Marquitos y Gento. Más tarde hubo otros muy significados, en especial Carlos Santillana, protagonista principal en la serie de remontadas europeas en el tiempo de la Quinta del Buitre. El gran referente, claro, es Gento, que me viene a la mente justo ahora que el puesto de extremo izquierdo en el equipo atrae tantas miradas. Vinicius había sido el mejor en ese puesto desde la retirada del glorioso cántabro, pero se nos está viniendo abajo. Aún no están demasiado lejos sus colosales partidos, con media docena de galopadas en cada tiempo, su insistencia en el peligro, su capacidad para repetir esfuerzos hasta el último minuto. Llegó sin capacidad para finalizar, no veía el pase ni era preciso ante el gol, pero con Ancelotti lo corrigió y llegó a destellar tanto que hasta su Balón de Plata (el mismo que le acaban de otorgar ahora a Mbappé) enfadó tanto a Florentino que suspendió el viaje colectivo a París pese a que había otros, y nada despreciables, premios para el club. Y a partir de aquello, ha ido cuesta abajo en la rodada. “¡Vinicius, Balón de Playa!” le gritan burla en los campos, mientras el Bernabéu ha empezado a distanciarse de él y a verle con antipatía, en especial desde su visible sabotaje al proyecto Xabi Alonso. Su juego ha decaído y sus actitudes han empezado a ser vistas como un problema para el Madrid. Su renovación desagradó a muchos. Pero he aquí que Diomande ha levantado la mano y dado el paso al frente. De sus pálidas y cortas intervenciones primerizas ha pasado a dar la pinta de jugadorazo, con desborde, disparo y solidaridad atrás. El tirón de pelo le ha dado una larga oportunidad de cuatro partidos. Ahora el problema ya no lo tiene el Madrid, sino Vinicius.

articles.title: How talking about Manchester United cycle of doom became an industry
articles.summary: Manchester United's struggles are pored over more than ever before - not least by former players.
articles.body:
Manchester United . More a high-volume content farm than a football club these days.

Michael Carrick's starring role in what has become one of the nation's favourite soap operas has been extended for at least another week, with the 45-year-old set to be in charge for Saturday's visit to Chelsea .

Good news - you'd think - for Carrick. But even better news for Amazon's All or Nothing camera crews, who have been given "unprecedented" access to document the behind-the-scenes goings-on at Old Trafford this season.

United fans will presumably be relieved when the football resumes on Saturday, if only to break up the constant stream of opinion for 90 minutes.

But while the wall-to-wall reporting of one of the world's biggest football clubs is hardly new, the unrelenting coverage from former players is a growing phenomenon.

It is easier to name the Manchester United legends who don't have a platform from which they scrutinise the club's every move than those that do - and it begs the question whether the club's demise has been industrialised into a content-creating machine.

Whether supporters feel comments from ex-players are damaging or not differs from fan to fan, but what cannot be denied is how difficult it is to escape their views.

Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville provided scathing on-air commentary during United's 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last Sunday, before conducting a post-match podcast in the Old Trafford gantry in which he accused some of their players of being unprofessional.

"There's a couple of them... I live in Manchester and they're not that professional, some of them," Neville stated.

"I've got no time for them. There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time. Don't eat the right things. Don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every single day."

But it's digital and streaming platforms that are re-defining a new age of analysis.

Neville launched The Overlap in 2021, and its success across video and podcast platforms has seen the channel become one of the most influential outlets in sports media.

On Tuesday, Wayne Rooney appeared on Neville's Manchester United -dedicated YouTube channel 'Stick to United' where he said Carrick's players "need a firework up their a***".

Neville has since hosted his own The Overlap show where he said managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good", while ex-United captain Roy Keane said Carrick and his backroom staff are "lucky boys" to still be in jobs.

Neville acquired a network of YouTube channels from United influencer Mark Goldbridge last summer, which has significantly increased the channel's coverage of the club.

Largely known for viral clips of his expletive-laden rants during streamed 'watchalongs' of their matches, Goldbridge's YouTube channels had amassed more than 3.7million subscribers.

Goldbridge - whose real name is Brent di Cesare - now co-hosts the 'Stick to United' show with Rooney, the club's record goalscorer.

But Neville, Rooney and Keane are far from the only ones setting the agenda.

Class of '92 pair Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt co-host their own podcast called 'The Good, The Bad & The Football'.

Before last season's Manchester derby at Old Trafford - Carrick's first home game in charge - Butt said City striker Erling Haaland would "pick Lisandro Martinez up and run with him", while Scholes said the Norway forward would "throw him in the net" after scoring.

United won the game 2-0, with Martinez putting in a stellar performance.

Asked about Scholes' comments after the match, the Argentine defender said: "Honestly, he can say whatever he wants. I told him already, if he wants to say something to me, he can come to wherever he wants. To my house, wherever. I don't care."

Asked during Thursday's news conference how he deals with the 'noise' from former team-mates and ex-players, Carrick said he avoids it as best he can.

"I don't see it really. I see the things that I need to see," he added.

"I don't look for it - it doesn't really help in any way.

"I've said it before, I care about what the supporters think. I care about what it feels like in the stadium, and them travelling to games for us, to come and see us and support us. I care about what we give them, and what we offer them, and what they see. I genuinely don't take any notice of anything else."

How Lineker and Neville became rival media moguls

'Fully committed' Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain

Sometimes managers need sacking for own good - Neville

Where once a low rating in a newspaper could anger players, they now have to deal with days of debate after a bad result or below-par performance.

Former manager Erik ten Hag recently alluded to the difficulty his Manchester United squad had dealing with the opinions of people like Neville and Rio Ferdinand, and said former players could be "more helpful" to the club.

"I did nice interviews with them both [Neville and Ferdinand], so it didn't hurt me. Of course, they have podcasts, they have their models," Ten Hag told The Athletic , external .

"Sometimes it's difficult for players. Some of them get affected by it, get annoyed by it.

"They achieved massive successes. But also, they can help the club more, help the players more. There should be two ways that they support it. But I think always the thing you most love, you most criticise."

Speaking on Ferdinand's podcast , external last summer, it was put to Neville he had been overly critical when covering his boyhood club.

"It's a balance though Rio, isn't it?" he told his former United team-mate.

"It's like, do I want [Manchester] City to win the league? I absolutely don't want City anywhere near the league title."

And he insisted "United are the hardest games I do".

"People might think that I'm more critical of United when they don't play well. Sometimes, over the last maybe 10 years, the balance, maybe I've not got it right," admitted Neville.

But, having won 18 major honours in 19 years at Old Trafford, few are better placed to judge the club than Neville.

"There was a banner in the first half [against Bournemouth ] that was held up in the Stretford End - 'standards'. They went a long time ago," he said last Sunday.

Like Neville, Butt also came through United's academy and said former players have the club's best interests at heart.

"When it goes bad, you can't cry and go, 'Oh, they're [ex-players] having a go at us'," explained Butt back in January.

"We love the football club. I've been a Manchester United fan since the age of six or seven, as long as I can remember. I'm not saying it to go, 'Let's stab everybody in the back'. I'm saying it because it is genuinely c**p."

While the club would rather be awash with positivity, negative coverage is consumed by a wider base that more regularly includes non- Manchester United fans.

It's difficult to apply a value to the club's popularity but United have remained one of the highest-grossing football clubs in world football since last winning the Premier League in 2013.

Much of their off-field success has been underscored by industry-leading commercial deals, as well as strong matchday revenue. Only Arsenal made more money from matchday revenue last season in the Premier League.

Former executive vice-chairman Ed Woodward angered supporters in 2018 when he said: "Playing performance doesn't really have a meaningful impact on what we can do on the commercial side of the business."

Being a constant source of attention is something that the club and supporters have regularly boasted about, too.

The 'hated, adored, never ignored' mantra regularly appears on banners at Old Trafford, while the club even released a clothing range that adorned the slogan.

It's fair to say, then, that the club are as guilty as anyone in capitalising on their global fame and ability to grab headlines.

articles.title: Inglaterra convoca al padre de Bellingham, "el Pelé del fútbol aficionado" por sus más de 700 goles
articles.standfirst: Mark Bellingham (1976) ha sido convocado para jugar con la selección de veteranos de Inglaterra para jugadores de 50 años o más
articles.summary: Mark Bellingham (1976) ha sido convocado para jugar con la selección de veteranos de Inglaterra para jugadores de 50 años o más
articles.body: El sargento Mark Bellingham (1976) , el padre de Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid) y Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), ha sido convocado para jugar con la selección inglesa de mayores de 50 años en un enfrentamiento contra Irlanda. El 'Daily Mail' destaca que la selección inglesa de veteranos (mayores de 50 años) es la actual campeona de la Copa del Mundo de veteranos, tras haber conquistado su noveno título en Tailandia a principios de este año. Con esta internacinalidad Mark Bellingham, que es conocido como el 'Pelé de las ligas no profesionales', será el tercer Bellingham internacional con Inglaterra. Jude ha sido 60 veces internacional absoluto con los 'Three Lions' y Jobe ya es internacional sub-21. Mark Bellingham (50 años) es un mito del fútbol no profesional inglés, en el que marcó más de 700 goles a lo largo de su trayectoria de 25 años por diversos clubes de categorías amateurs. El padre de los Bellingham, que se retiró en 2017, fue un talentoso delantero que jugó en al menos 20 clubes distintos, entre los que destacan Leamington, Stourbridge y Sutton Coldfield Town. Mark Bellingham es seguidor del Southend United y Jude presenció sus primeros partidos de fútbol en Roots Hall. "Hablamos de héroes futbolísticos, y mi padre fue, por así decirlo, el primero para mí. Cuando vas a verle jugar cada semana en categorías no profesionales —ya sabes, no es la Premier League ni nada por el estilo—, ver su forma de jugar y el ambiente que se vivía hizo que me enamorara del fútbol. Así que, probablemente, él fue mi primer héroe... Después de las primeras veces, empecé a prestar más atención a los partidos, al ambiente... y como él marcaba goles, lo veías celebrándolos y cosas así; entonces piensas: 'Ojalá fuera yo'", reconoció Jude Bellingham en una reciente entrevista. Mark Bellingham trabajó como sargento de policía antes de convertirse en agente de fútbol y dedicarse por completo a las carreras de sus hijos, a los que sigue por toda Europa. Él fue el encargado de negociar el traspaso de Jude al Real Madrid en 2023 y el traspaso de Jobe al Borussia Dortmund en 2025. Mark y Denise, madre de Jude y Jobe, están separados y mantienen una buena relación.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Women's football attendances have stalled
articles.summary: Average Women's Super League attendances surged by 192% in the season after the Lionesses' Euro 2022 triumph, but the boom has stalled.
articles.body:
Average Women's Super League attendances surged by 192% in the season after the Lionesses' Euro 2022 triumph, but the speed of the boom has stalled.

Median crowds have risen by just 166 fans - from 3,070 in 2023-24 to 3,236 in 2025-2026 - according to a 2026 report from YouGov and architecture firm Populous , external which surveyed 2,000 fans.

Some of the biggest fixtures are now attracting significantly smaller attendances.

Arsenal against Manchester United at Emirates Stadium fell from 46,603 in 2024-25 to 29,853 this season, while Chelsea v Arsenal dropped from 34,302 to 19,349 over the same period.

The Gunners, who averaged 34,000 at the Emirates last season - almost four times the next-highest club, Chelsea, and higher than eight Premier League sides, , external had just 19,546 for their October match against Birmingham City.

There are bright spots, including a sold-out 4,000-ticket Arsenal away allocation at Tottenham for the first time, but the wider trend for some matches is clear.

Manchester United against Manchester City was hosted at Leigh Village in October with a crowd of 5,361. The same fixture was held at Old Trafford in March 2026 with 24,983 fans.

A spokesperson for WSL Football told BBC Sport there was "strong demand for the women's game".

So what is behind the decline? Marketing, scheduling, matchday experience, stadium design, product or something else?

Families v loyal fans - can women's football attract both?

When supporters were asked what mattered most to their enjoyment of a women's football match in the report, a "welcoming, family-friendly environment" ranked above team success and the quality of on-pitch performance for both established and potential fans.

The research found only 15% of fans who have attended a women's match in the past five years do so at least monthly.

Meanwhile, 43% describe themselves as casual followers who engage more with major international tournaments than domestic club football, while just 10% identify as devoted supporters.

The findings suggest there is a possible matchday "experience gap" in the domestic game, with some clubs seeking to address it through family-friendly initiatives.

However, some fans have voiced their frustration at the family-friendly marketing.

Tottenham fan Dakota said "I'm almost glad I can't make it" in relation to a Spurs social media advert about the north London derby, which listed DJs, drinks, face painting and freestylers.

She added: "We'll never grow as a women's club if the entire marketing is for kids and families rather than young adults with disposable income."

Another Spurs fan, Rosewen, had similar views: "They can offer attractions to tempt people through the gates but we're losing sight of football and the importance of winning."

On the recent low crowd for the north London derby, one fan wrote on X: "Attendances across the WSL are down so this isn't a Spurs specific issue. However, the club has used a one-dimensional family-friendly marketing strategy for years."

Brighton took a similar family focused approach for their October match against West Ham at the Amex, promoting a "Saturday Spooktacular" with attractions including a haunted house, face-painting, hair braiding, costume competitions and other activities taking up the majority of the advert.

How does scheduling impact crowd numbers?

Premier League football has long owned the 3pm Saturday slot, while the WSL has varied kick-off times, making it harder for fans to establish a regular routine.

Inconsistent kick-off times emerged as a common concern when BBC Sport asked why attendances were falling.

Arsenal fan Sue said: "It's the constant changing of the game times and travel issues. I had six lots of tickets for Arsenal games last season. For three matches, the day and time changed and for another three, there were bus replacements for trains.

"These issues put families off. WSL needs regular days/time slots to attract consistent fans."

Victoria agreed: "Scheduling is dreadful. They need to stick to Sunday afternoon where possible. I get fed up of all the late changes to day/times. Consistency is key to its success."

The October north London derby at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium kicked off at 12:45 BST, with Arsenal's men playing Everton later the same day, forcing some fans to choose between the two.

The attendance at the women's match was 13,719, less than half the 28,852 who watched the same fixture in 2024.

A WSL Football spokesperson said: "Despite challenges with fixture scheduling and stadium availability there is strong demand for the women's game, and the wider picture remains positive, with more fans engaging with women's football content, growing revenues and cumulative attendances exceeding one million across the past three seasons."

Attempts to attract new audiences to women's football have sometimes misfired.

The Sky Sports TikTok channel Halo was shut down within 48 hours after criticism that its pink branding and lifestyle-focused content felt patronising.

Similar concerns followed a Women's League Cup draw hosted by influencer GK Barry .

Disney+'s coverage of the Women's Champions League also faced challenge for including gimmicks such as a dog and a vegetable platter.

The debate highlights a wider challenge for broadcasters: how do you attract new audiences without alienating existing ones?

Does Scott's Disney+ exit unmask wider issue in coverage of women's game?

One fan told BBC Sport a lack of jeopardy makes WSL matches less appealing: "Attendances need to be taken in context. If a match is a 'dead rubber' less people will turn up against a game with something on it. In the Premier League most games have competition for something. WSL has less European places and fewer relegation places. Too many 'nothing' games."

This view was echoed by London City Lionesses owner Michele Kang, who said at the World Football Summit in Madrid earlier this year: "If you look at Spain, France and Germany, the competitive balance is not quite there yet."

Barcelona's appearance in seven of the past eight Women's Champions League finals supports this.

Home venues vary across the WSL, from Manchester United's 12,000-spectator Leigh Sports Village and Brighton's 6,134-seat Broadfield Stadium to Arsenal's 60,000-seat Emirates and Chelsea and Everton's 40,000-capacity grounds.

Larger stadiums offer room for growth but can feel empty, while smaller venues often generate atmosphere at the expense of capacity and facilities.

One supporter told BBC Sport: "For many families of fans of the larger clubs hosting WSL games in the main stadiums allowed cheap access to visit iconic stadia.

"But now most people have been to Old Trafford, Emirates, Etihad etc, so you see the drop-off as the novelty has worn off."

Brighton hope to address this with plans for Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium, a £75-80m, 10,000-capacity ground next to the Amex.

The club say they will provide a permanent home for the women's team, while being designed specifically for female players, families and first-time fans.

CEO Paul Barber said a purpose-built stadium was important to give "respect and focus" to the women's team.

The move aligns with the WSL's "world-first design guidelines", which argue stadiums have historically been built for men's football and need to better serve female players and fans.

Brighton plan Europe's first purpose-built £80m women's stadium

Four years on from Euro 2022, the WSL's challenge is not attracting interest but turning occasional visitors into regular supporters and helping fans build tribalism.

Despite remaining one of the more affordable sports for fans to attend, women's football is likely not immune to the impact of the UK's cost-of-living pressures, which may also influence crowd numbers.

Some believe clubs can cater to different audiences at the same time.

One fan told BBC Sport: "Matchday doesn't need to be either/or. London City had a fan zone aimed at children ahead of last week's match with Everton.

"They also had a post-match Oktoberfest aimed at an older age group. Different marketing for different audiences for the same matchday."

Former England international Ellen White told BBC's Women's Football Fallout: "The beautiful thing about women's football is that it is for everyone.

"I don't think it's about dismissing any of our audiences. I think it's about finding the marketing strategies that will grow our game and sell stadiums out."

As professional pathways produce more elite players, standards, product and competitiveness should rise.

Similarly, the first generation of fans to grow up with regular exposure to women's football should build fandom that help attendances boom.

A spokesperson from WSL Football supported this and said: "Women's football is still at an early stage and growth is not linear.

"We are still learning about the fanbase and we are working proactively with clubs on ways to increase the visibility of their women's teams and build awareness of matches."

articles.title: Camacho advierte a Mbappé y al Madrid por su polémica con China: "Imagino que tendrán buenos abogados"
articles.summary: José Antonio Camacho, que fue seleccionador de China de 2011 a 2013, habló en el programa 'El Partidazo de COPE' sobre la polémica con China por el comentario de Kylian Mbappé sobre un meme de Mao Zedong.
articles.body: José Antonio Camacho, que fue seleccionador de China de 2011 a 2013, habló en el programa 'El Partidazo de COPE' sobre la polémica con China por el comentario de Kylian Mbappé sobre un meme de Mao Zedong. El técnico murciano le explicó a Juanma Castaño que, aunque no recibió un manual de instrucciones sobre temas prohibidos, sí mantuvo reuniones con altas esferas, como el ministro de Deporte, que le dejaron clara la filosofía del país. "Ellos siempre te dicen que te tienes que adaptar a las normas suyas, a la manera suya y a todo lo que ellos hacen. Ellos piensan que son los amos del mundo en todos los aspectos, y no es fácil", reconoció. José Antonio Camacho le ha recomendado al Real Madrid y a Mbappé tener "buenos abogados", porque en su experiencia, "ellos cortan de inmediato, y ya te apañarás con FIFA, con UEFA o con quien tenga que ser pertinente".

articles.title: André Almeida y el desafío del Racing ante la vuelta del Madrid al Sardinero: “No tenemos miedo a nadie”
articles.standfirst: El centrocampista portugués aseguró en 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA que el conjunto cántabro confía en dar la sorpresa ante los blancos, destacó las virtudes de su equipo y elogió la capacidad de Mourinho para motivar a sus jugadores
articles.summary: El centrocampista portugués aseguró en 'La Tribu' de Radio MARCA que el conjunto cántabro confía en dar la sorpresa ante los blancos, destacó las virtudes de su equipo y elogió la capacidad de Mourinho para motivar a sus jugadores
articles.body: El Racing de Santander espera al Real Madrid en El Sardinero con una mezcla de ilusión y ambición. El partido del domingo supone una cita especialmente señalada para el conjunto cántabro tras su regreso a Primera División. André Almeida pasó por La Tribu de Radio MARCA para explicar cómo prepara el equipo la visita de los blancos y por qué considera posible dar la sorpresa. “Son once hombres contra once hombres y todo puede pasar. Yo estoy confiado en que podemos ganar”, aseguró el centrocampista portugués. Aunque reconoce la calidad de la plantilla madridista, Almeida no quiere que el Racing se sienta inferior antes de empezar: “Todos los que están en Madrid son buenos jugadores, pero yo no tengo miedo a nadie”. Almeida cree que el estilo del Racing puede poner en dificultades al equipo de José Mourinho. Su principal argumento es la pelota: el conjunto cántabro quiere atacar, tener la iniciativa y evitar que el rival encuentre espacios para correr. “Creo que tenemos un estilo de juego que nos puede venir bien contra el Real Madrid”, defendió. “Si tenemos el balón podemos hacer daño”, añadió. Almeida, sin embargo, sabe que no bastará con firmar un buen encuentro. Considera necesario que el Madrid no esté especialmente acertado, porque sus individualidades pueden desequilibrar cualquier acción. También recordó los problemas que han encontrado los blancos en algunas salidas esta temporada para explicar por qué nadie en Santander da el encuentro por perdido. Almeida siguió con atención el último Clásico y confesó que el rendimiento blanco le sorprendió. “Yo esperaba que el Barcelona, jugando en casa, iba a ser más imponente”, reconoció. Pero el Real Madrid ofreció una respuesta que no imaginaba: “El Real Madrid me ha sorprendido mucho”. El centrocampista atribuyó parte de esa reacción al entrenador portugués: “Mourinho siempre pone sangre en los jugadores”. La entrevista también recuperó el interés que el Barcelona mostró por Almeida cuando todavía pertenecía al Valencia. Aquella operación no llegó a concretarse y el portugués reflexionó sobre las dificultades que encuentran los futbolistas para decidir su futuro: “Tienes que estar bien acompañado y hacer bien las cosas para el futuro estar en tus manos también”. Advirtió además del peso de las cláusulas y de las decisiones que toman los clubes. En el césped le espera otro portugués, Bernardo Silva, al que considera un referente. “Es un gran jugador, mucha calidad, es un ejemplo para mí”, afirmó, antes de expresar su deseo de ganar ese duelo. Sobre Vinicius también fue claro: si está motivado, “es de los mejores del mundo”, por lo que considera que su presencia complicaría todavía más el partido. Almeida ya ha comprobado cómo se vive la llegada del Madrid en Santander. “La gente, por ser el Madrid, ya me pidió entradas”, contó con humor. Incluso los vecinos de su zona le han preguntado por localidades, aunque el club solo le facilita cinco y debe reservarlas para su familia. El entusiasmo, eso sí, no cambia la prioridad del vestuario: sumar puntos para mantenerse en Primera. “Estamos haciendo bien las cosas, ir partido a partido”, explicó, aunque admitió que fuera de casa les está costando más. Almeida cree que la segunda vuelta será decisiva, pero antes espera que El Sardinero empuje al Racing hacia un triunfo de enorme repercusión.

articles.title: Tony Pulis column: Why managers must put their own fitness first
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains why Vincent Kompany's health scare was a reminder that management takes its toll physically and mentally
articles.body:
A lot has changed for football managers over the past few decades but Vincent Kompany's recent health scare was a reminder it is still an all-consuming occupation that takes its toll physically and mentally.

From the tragic death of Scotland manager Jock Stein after a World Cup qualifier against Wales in 1985, to the different heart issues suffered by Graeme Souness, Sir Alex Ferguson, Gerard Houllier, Joe Kinnear and Harry Redknapp down the years, I've always been aware of the dangers of my job.

It is 25 years since then Leicester boss Dave Bassett and Bolton manager Sam Allardyce took part in an experiment that saw them wired up to heart monitors during a game between the teams, and both their heart rates reached critical levels.

It's not just during games when management can have an adverse effect on your health, either.

The stress you are under is relentless and you have to find a way of looking after yourself. Fortunately this was something I realised very early on in my management career.

'In the early days, my management of myself was really poor'

I had worked under and alongside managers for my entire working life as a player and then coach, but it was only when I got my first management job - at Bournemouth in 1992 - that I realised the workload you undertake and just how time consuming and stressful a job it is.

In those days, and in fact throughout my whole career, I wanted to be the person who made all the footballing decisions at my club.

That meant I did everything from scouting players to signing the ones I wanted, and organised my staff at every level from first-team to the reserve and youth teams, all within the club's financial restraints.

I saw the first-team performances as being my main responsibility so I never wavered from my work on the training ground either, coaching a certain way that suited the players and gave them the best chance of winning games - which would ultimately determine my future.

All of the above was generally the way most English clubs were run so it was not just me doing it. But the demands were relentless, and I had to learn how to look after myself properly to cope.

During those early days, my management of myself personally was really poor.

It starts with your diet. At that time I would be driving up and down the motorway to watch players, trying to find a fish and chip shop or fuelled only by a half-time pie or a sandwich from a local shop.

I was young and could deal with it, so it never crossed my mind that I wasn't eating well or getting the exercise I needed to retain my own fitness levels.

But, at the same time, the pressure on the team to win games ultimately fell on my shoulders so the pressure of being the person responsible for results and performances every week really built up.

I had never realised how stressful that part of management was until we started to lose a few games and every bit of criticism was directed on to my lap.

That part has not changed for managers now.

They may have less to do with the way their clubs are run now but they still have to deal with people they have never met criticising their ability to do a job they love to media outlets, without taking into consideration any other factors that might be contributing to those performances and results.

That's why it's so stressful. All the arrows and guns are pointed in your direction, and you have no way of protecting yourself, apart from by winning games.

'A release valve that was an important part of my routine'

Many a young manager will have experienced these factors, which could and would affect their health and wellbeing.

The turning point for me came when I spoke to an Australian triathlete just before I left Bournemouth in 1994.

His advice was pretty blunt and straightforward. He told me doing my job was physically hampering my own fitness levels - but more worrying were the stress levels that came with it, because they could have a major effect on my life itself.

It was only after having that conversation that I realised the compromises I was making for my career at the cost of my own health.

I came to the conclusion that in my next job, if I got one, I would dedicate myself to a more manageable lifestyle and put my own fitness first.

I decided I would work out early every morning before breakfast at the club I managed, so I could then dedicate the rest of my day to my work.

Yes, there were days I would be empty and would only walk and stretch, but generally I stuck to that rule and worked hard to keep on top of myself physically.

At Gillingham in 1999, I decided to run a marathon - my first London Marathon - which got me focused during the season in respect of my physical health.

That was my first challenge of many I have taken on for charity down the years. I have also cycled from John O' Groats to Land's End, walked up Mount Kilimanjaro, and rowed from Tower Bridge to the Eiffel Tower.

All of this exercise also helped my stress levels, especially in respect of sleeping. Being tired going to bed really helped my sleeping hours and meant I was never kept awake worrying about what was going wrong at work.

There were other ways I looked after my mental health too. Even as the internet exploded, I have never read any press, good or bad, about me or my team.

I always worked as hard I could at every club I was with, and picked good staff who I was able to confide in, but I was able to switch off too, thanks to my family.

I've written in previous columns about my routine after games and how I would often drive home to the south coast on a Saturday night, reflecting on our result and starting my preparation for our next game.

But Sundays were always about spending all day with the family.

Whether it was watching my son Anthony playing football as a young boy, or just being around the children full stop, that was how I relaxed and that day with them became a release valve which was an important part of my routine.

When I speak to young managers now, I give them the same advice I followed.

You have to maintain your enthusiasm for looking after yourself, because this is the time when you will need it the most. Under the constant stress you will put yourself under, it is dangerous not to.

But, while everyone knows the risks of the job, many are prepared to take them. I always was.

Years ago, managers' health was never much of a concern to clubs - we probably drank too much and ate too many of the wrong foods, at all hours of the day and night, but that was just part of the lifestyle that went with it.

Now, there is lots more support - the League Managers' Association offers frequent health testing under its 'Fit To Manage' programme, and most clubs' medical staff will now ensure that not only are their players properly looked after, the coaching staff is too.

A manager's life can still be a lonely place, but thankfully the help available is on a different level to where it was at the start of my career.

Tony Pulis was speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan.

articles.title: FPL gameweek nine tips: Is it time to invest in Bournemouth assets?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers in gameweek nine.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's Fantasy Premier League expert FPL Heisenberg gives his answers to some of the biggest dilemmas facing managers heading into gameweek nine.

Is now the time to invest in Bournemouth assets?

Yes, I think so. They face Leeds at home in gameweek nine, followed by a very appealing run of fixtures over the next few gameweeks.

Marcus Tavernier (£6.4m) is my favourite pick. He's been attracting plenty of attention after recent performances and offers a good combination of goal threat and creativity from midfield.

Evanilson (£6.2m) is another one I'd consider. He's a decent budget forward who should get opportunities to score in this run of fixtures. If you're after a cheaper route into Bournemouth 's attack, he's worth a look.

Antonio Silva (£5.0m) is my defender of choice as he's great for defensive contributions, but I won't be rushing to triple up on the Cherries.

Should we be buying Jackson after his double against Man City?

Nicolas Jackson (£6.7m) is certainly an interesting option after a strong run of recent form - scoring four in his past four Premier League matches.

He looks to be finding his feet at Aston Villa and he's an appealing alternative to some of the other budget forwards in the game.

Aston Villa face Fulham at home in gameweek nine, which is the start of a very nice run of fixtures to back him in.

My only concern is his minutes. There's a slight risk of him being hooked early, especially with Villa juggling Champions League football and promising young striker Brian Madjo (£5.4m) back from injury.

However, with his recent form and price in mind, he's definitely worth considering.

Is Haaland still the obvious captain choice?

Yes, absolutely. Erling Haaland (£15.7m) remains the standout captaincy option for me, even after Manchester City 's first Premier League defeat of the season.

He scored again against Aston Villa in gameweek eight and continues to be the player I'd back to deliver the biggest points haul in any given match.

This doesn't mean you have to captain him every single gameweek of course - there will be opportunities to look elsewhere at times. However, he's the only reliable premium asset in the game right now.

Joao Pedro (£7.8m) is an easy sell following Xabi Alonso's comments ruling him out for weeks.

Some may be thinking of holding the Chelsea forward through his injury and simply benching him. I can see why this is tempting, because when he's fit, he's one of the best assets in the game.

However, we don't know how long this could go on for, so I won't be holding him hoping for a speedy recovery.

Another reason he's an easy sell is the mid-priced forwards are actually enticing right now.

Alternatives such as Jackson and Evanilson have excellent form and favourable forthcoming fixtures.

The likes of Dominic Calvert Lewin (£6.1m), Thierno Barry (£5.6m) or if you have the money Alexander Isak (£9.1m) are all worth considering, too.

It's likely I'll be selling Rayan Cherki (£8.0m) this week. He's clearly a talented player, but his minutes are becoming a real concern and there are better options available at a cheaper price.

He was substituted at half-time against Aston Villa in gameweek eight, having also struggled for consistent minutes in previous games. When you're spending that much on a midfielder, you want someone who's likely to play 80-90 minutes regularly.

I'll be looking at the likes of Tavernier as a cheaper alternative, freeing up funds to strengthen elsewhere in my team.

Cherki could easily punish sellers if he starts and hauls, but I'd rather back a player with more reliable minutes. For me, it's time to sell.

I'm not looking to sell my Arsenal players just because they face Liverpool away in gameweek nine.

David Raya (£6.2m) and Riccardo Calafiori (£6m) remain quality defensive options, but the Liverpool fixture does make a clean sheet less likely than usual.

After that, Arsenal face Hull , Newcastle , Manchester City and Brentford . There are opportunities in that mixed fixture run, and Arsenal being one of the best teams in the league makes them favourites going into the majority of games.

If you've got Arsenal defensive assets, I'd be happy to hold rather than spend transfers trying to chase fixtures. If Calafiori is injured, I'll probably just bench him against Liverpool and hope he's ready for Hull at home the following gameweek.

However, I wouldn't necessarily be buying Arsenal assets this week as several other teams offering more attractive short-term fixtures.

I'd prioritise those options before bringing in another Arsenal defender.

articles.title: Liverpool vs Arsenal: Andoni Iraola's side must beat the Premier League champions to be in the title race, says Paul Merson
articles.summary: Champions Arsenal head to Anfield with a six-point lead over Liverpool but have not won there in the league since 2012; Andoni Iraola has beaten Mikel Arteta three times in his last four meetings; watch Liverpool vs Arsenal live on Sky Sports this Sunday, kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
Andoni Iraola's side host the champions live on Sky Sports' Super Sunday , kick-off 4.30pm, with Liverpool six points behind joint-leaders Arsenal and Man City.

Iraola managed three victories over Arteta's Arsenal in his final four meetings as Bournemouth head coach, but the Reds boss lost his first heavyweight clash at Anfield against City earlier this month.

With Liverpool on a five-game winning run and Arsenal unbeaten in six, read below for the Magic Man's thoughts about the game of the weekend...

'If Liverpool want a title race, they have to beat Arsenal'

Liverpool are starting to cook a little bit, but they have got to win this Sunday if they want to be in the Premier League title race.

If they don't win, they stay six points behind at least and still have to go to the Emirates.

You're then asking Arsenal to lose two football matches without you losing one. And given Liverpool will lose more games this season, you're then asking Arsenal to lose three or four games for the rest of the season. That's a lot of games.

But at the same time, it's also must-not-lose for Liverpool as they still need to stay on track for the Champions League places.

If Arsenal go and win against Liverpool, that could nearly be it for the Premier League title. You then start to think: who's going to go and beat them?

This Sunday is one of only three or four difficult games Arsenal have got this season.

Those games are Man City away, Liverpool away, Chelsea away when they're hot, plus the likes of Brighton and Brentford who if you beat, you know they'll do you a favour by beating your rivals later in the season.

The last time Arsenal won a game at Liverpool in the league was in 2012, I couldn't believe it when I saw that stat. Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they won at Anfield and now he's the manager!

That history makes it a must-not-lose for Arsenal as well. Just don't get beat. But if Arsenal go and win at Anfield, you go: wow.

'Saka injury a blow ahead of crucial month'

What a November Arsenal have, by the way. They've got a hard month, including the start of December.

You'll know by December 13 if Arsenal will win the Premier League. Because there's a saying: after the hard games, come the easy games.

If Bukayo Saka is injured for this period, he's going to be missed. People say he isn't playing well, I think he's a decision-maker - he constantly makes those right decisions week in, week out.

Now there's Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze coming in and playing in his place. It's all well and good them coming in and playing for a couple, then sitting out for a couple - but when you're asking them to play six to eight weeks on the trot, that's a real tester. That's where it might take its toll.

But that might be a good thing for them. They know they're going to play and they can relax and go and express themselves, which is what you want - especially with Eze. And especially now that Max Dowman is set to be suspended.

articles.title: Alexander Isak: Why keeping Sweden striker fit and firing is key to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool revival
articles.summary: Alexander Isak heads into Sunday's showdown with champions Arsenal having scored in three straight Premier League games for first time since January 2025; watch Liverpool vs Arsenal on Sunday on Sky Sports Premier League from 3.30pm; kick-off 4.30pm
articles.body:
Isak's neatly-taken goal in Liverpool's 2-0 win over an in-form Brighton at Anfield on Sunday means the Swede has now registered in three straight Premier League games for first time since January 2025, when he went on an eight-match scoring streak for Newcastle.

What was equally encouraging for head coach Andoni Iraola was the way Isak and fellow £100m-plus recruit Bradley Barcola, operating on the right-hand side of the front three on this occasion, linked up for his goal as the France forward broke clear before locating Isak where he is most effective - in the six-yard box, between the width of the posts.

This was always the vision of Richard Hughes and Michael Edwards, the men who brought Isak to the club last summer for that British-record fee, as well as Florian Wirtz for a similarly hefty outlay, as they looked to build on the previous season's title win by investing heavily in just one or two marquee signings, rather than follow Arsenal's approach and spread the finances out so as to build a bigger, more durable squad.

After Edwards's departure in July, it was Hughes who then got the Barcola deal over the line before his own Anfield exit, as Liverpool looked to double down on their policy of signing smaller, technical players at a time when the Premier League was becoming increasingly physical.

But perhaps the duo's vision for a post-Mohamed Salah front line is now starting to be realised - never more so than with Isak.

The signs looked promising for the player after an encouraging showing for Sweden at last summer's World Cup, followed by more impressive displays in pre-season for the Reds, form which he carried over into this campaign.

Isak poached his first goal of the new season in the 2-2 home draw with Nottingham Forest in August, one of six in his seven league outings so far, leaving him just one behind Erling Haaland at the top of the Premier League scoring chart.

And his overall importance to the team can be seen by the fact the 27-year-old has scored in every one of their league wins to date, while only Victor Munoz among his team-mates has more than one top-flight goal this season.

Iraola, though, is not so worried about how many goals his big-money striker gets, more how he can help the team win with his pressing from the front.

"He's a massive player for us," Iraola told Sky Sports in September. "Probably my demands will not be about the goals, I know that [if] he's fit, he's in good shape, he's going to produce the numbers.

"My fights with him are more about other stuff, about how to help the team in all the situations."

And it was no coincidence that despite his recent fine run in front of goal, the Liverpool head coach was still banging that same drum ahead of Arsenal's visit to Anfield on Super Sunday.

"I think Alex feels the trust of everyone," Iraola reiterated in midweek. "Everyone trusts if he moves into good positions he will score goals.

"But I always tell him he has to help us so we can give you the chances, and I think he understands that necessity. I hope that can continue at the same level."

However, it is not just the eye test Isak is passing, with the Sweden international understandably now moving much freer after last season's injury woes and finally beginning to look like the player Liverpool thought they were buying, but statistically his on-pitch numbers also point to a vast improvement in his attacking output.

For one thing, Isak is taking a shot more per league game this season, 3.15 compared to 2.18, which probably explains why his xG per 90 has also doubled from 0.33 to 0.67 this campaign, while his strike rate of 0.95 goals per 90 minutes is second only to Haaland.

Among fellow top-flight strikers, only Haaland [24.1] has had fewer touches per game this season than Isak's 24.6, although like the Norwegian goal poacher, when a chance falls his way, he tends to bury it.

And those metrics are all tracking with his best scoring campaign in England, when Isak managed 27 goals in just 42 games in all competitions in his last season at St James' Park.

"He is massively important because Liverpool are not a great goalscoring team right now," was Jamie Carragher's assessment of just how reliant his former club now are on Isak from an attacking point of view.

"Besides him, who else is going to score the goals? Victor Munoz has got a couple, but Isak has made a great start, in complete contrast to last season, when he was injured.

"We've still not probably seen the full version of Isak that we saw at Newcastle, but I think that will come with more games, repetition of training sessions with Iraola and maybe we'll see the best of him in the second half of the season.

"But he's getting goals and he needs to get goals because there's aren't too many players around him getting goals for Liverpool."

It goes without saying, then, that Iraola and his medical team must now manage Isak's minutes given his own indifferent injury record and with fellow striker Hugo Ekitike still recovering from a long-term Achilles injury and not set to return until next year.

As such, the Reds boss often looks to replace Isak up front with Lewis Koumas towards the end of games, even more so after he was forced to miss the 3-0 home loss to Man City with a thigh problem suffered on international duty with Sweden.

Injuries have been a running theme for the Swede from the first day he joined the club, as they also were at times in his three seasons at Newcastle, and he arrived at Anfield having gone on strike and missed an entire pre-season in a bid to to push through the move.

That meant Isak was playing catch-up right from the start, and he missed four games with abductor pain in October and November before being sidelined for 106 days after his left leg was fractured in a challenge at Tottenham before Christmas.

When Isak did finally return in May, he was out for almost three weeks with more abductor issues and muscle strains to complete a miserable debut campaign on Merseyside that yielded just three league goals.

The combination of trying to get fit, while at the same time dealing with the huge weight of expectations that come with moving to the champions with a massive price tag at a time when the team was imploding, understandably proved a lot for a player who is naturally shy and retiring.

But with Isak's fitness now restored, and Liverpool gradually rediscovering their mojo again under their new head coach, in many ways this is like a new Anfield beginning for the Swede.

And with the champions in town this weekend, the club who were interested in signing him in January 2025, the striker has a chance to further show why he is now such an integral part of Iraola's Reds revival.

articles.title: Duncan Ferguson: Can Glentoran cause an upset in Scotsman's first game?
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks ahead to Duncan Ferguson's first game in charge of Glentoran against league leaders Coleraine on Friday.
articles.body:
Duncan Ferguson's highly anticipated first game as Glentoran boss will come six days later than first expected, but it will be a real baptism of fire for the former Everton striker as his side face leaders Coleraine.

As first games go there are few tougher than taking on the Bannsiders at their Showgrounds home in a game under the Friday night lights that will be live on BBC iPlayer and BBC Sport website.

While Coleraine did suffer their sole defeat of the season at home to a resurgent Linfield last month, they have since bounced back in style to win their next four and open up a two-point gap over the Blues, which can be extended with a win on Friday.

With the Glens' game against Ballymena United on Saturday postponed because of a waterlogged pitch, Ferguson opted to make the trip to Seaview to see Ruaidhri Higgins' side dispatch 10-man Crusaders 5-0 for himself.

That will have given him plenty of food for thought as to how to combat the in-form table toppers as he embarks on the latest chapter of his young managerial career.

Ferguson will 'boost profile of league' - Higgins

I'll give Glens everything, vows new boss Ferguson

All eyes on Ferguson in huge Showgrounds tussle

Glentoran are 14 points off Coleraine after a poor start to the season, but they are unbeaten in their past five games in the league following a 2-1 loss at the Oval against the Bannsiders.

A run that included four wins and a draw under joint interim managers Tim McCann and Paddy McCourt has helped the Glens up to fourth in the table.

A precious victory at the Showgrounds would move them level on points with Larne and send out a strong statement that Ferguson can handle the Irish Premiership, despite his limited knowledge of the league.

Ferguson, whose previous short stints as a manager came at Forest Green Rovers and Inverness, has had a week and a half to prepare his side for this fixture following the stunning announcement of his arrival on 19 October and the postponement of the Ballymena game.

In his first press conference he spoke about ensuring his team is one that will "really run, run and run".

He acknowledged that while they have the joint best defensive record in the league, having shipped just 10 goals in their 12 games, the Glens have "lacked in creating chances" and therefore need to play "attacking football".

The return to full fitness of star striker Pat Hoban should help Ferguson's side, who have scored just 16 goals this season, 15 fewer than Coleraine.

All eyes will be on 'Big Dunc' at the Showgrounds, with even Coleraine boss Higgins acknowledging that his team "might be a bit of a sideshow" given the attention and expectation surrounding the Scotsman.

Whatever the result it is set to be a memorable Irish League moment and Ferguson's fortunes at the club will be an intriguing subplot for the rest of the domestic season.

articles.title: Bordalás: “Nos hemos enfrentado a un equipo de la sexta categoría que no es profesional y nos pasó por encima la primera media hora"
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón analiza duramente el pase a la siguiente ronda de Copa del Rey
articles.summary: El técnico azulón comparecía tras la victoria y el pase a la siguiente ronda de Copa del Rey
articles.body: El entrenador del Getafe, José Bordalás, comparecía tras el encuentro frente a la UB Lebrijana. El técnico alicantino señaló no estar “contento” después de que el cuadro local, de sexta categoría, se pusiera 2-0 por delante: “No estoy contento, no merecimos pasar”, señaló el entrenador azulón, que admitió que el cuadro dirigido por Ceballos fue superior. Inicio de la Lebrijana: “Felicitamos a la Lebrijana, ha hecho un gran partido, nos han recibido fenomenal, nos han tratado muy bien. Han hecho un muy buen partido, han sido superiores a nosotros, sobre todo la primera media hora, se pusieron por delante de manera justa. Nosotros nos encontramos con dos goles en el tramo final del primer tiempo. No tenemos nada que celebrar, no hemos sido superiores a la Lebrijana. Continúa y ya a pensar en LaLiga, que es lo que tenemos el domingo”. Sensación: “No estoy contento porque creo que no merecíamos pasar, no tengo nada más que comentar, nos hemos enfrentado a un equipo de la sexta categoría que no es profesional y nos pasó por encima la primera media hora. No lo podemos permitir. Se ha impuesto ser profesionales y tener más capacidad a nivel físico, pero en muchos momentos fueron superiores”. Los dos goles encajados: “Han sido dos balones a balón parado. El domingo recibimos tres. Es un tema de concentración, es un tema de querer y de atención. No nos pueden marcar dos goles a balón parado y en el segundo tiempo han tenido otro que no remataron y nos pudieron marcar gol. Tenemos que trabajar y corregir. Centrarnos en el siguiente compromiso y saber que tenemos que mejorar muchísimo”. Relación con el Getafe: “Mi relación con el club y el presidente es fantástica, está clara. Es evidente, no hay ningún tipo de problema”. Punto de inflexión: “Siempre confías que sí, pero los jugadores no pueden estar contentos, al igual que yo. Tenemos que mejorar. Sirve para coger minutos jugadores que han jugado menos, que vienen de lesión. Todos los partidos te sirven para sacar conclusiones positivas y está claro que somos conscientes de que tenemos que mejorar. No tenemos nada que celebrar hoy, centrarnos en el Sevilla, que va a ser tremendamente complicado, ha confeccionado una plantilla competitiva, va a ser difícil”.

articles.title: Packers’ Watson makes improbable ‘Thursday Night Football’ return after mid-game trip to hospital
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson had himself a night to remember in the team’s 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on “Thursday Night Football.”
articles.body: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson had himself a night to remember in the team’s 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers on “Thursday Night Football.” The 27-year-old finished with a team-high eight receptions for 113 yards, got to welcome the Milwaukee Brewers to Lambeau Field following their first World Series title win 24 hours earlier, and completed a mid-game trip to the hospital. In the second quarter, Watson made a 53-yard catch that injured his chest when Panthers cornerback Will Lee III made a diving stop. Lee was also injured on the play and carted off the field with a hamstring injury. Lee, a rookie fourth-round pick, did not return to the game. Watson was taken out of the stadium by ambulance to a local hospital for reported “precautionary reasons” before returning via ambulance and being greeted by a raucous ovation from the Lambeau faithful after the Packers extended their lead to 27-10 in the third quarter. The 2022 second-round pick out of North Dakota State returned to the game, where he had two more receptions as the Packers were able to fend off a late comeback attempt by Carolina. After the game, Watson acknowledged that the experience was “tough” and expressed his thoughts on going to the hospital. “It was tough. Honestly, I never wanted to go,” Watson told the Prime broadcast. “I was hoping that they would let me off. I said I was kinda feeling better once I kinda caught my breath. But I mean, they said there was a couple of signs that made them have to take me over there. “It is what it is. I was just praying that it was good enough to where I could come back out here. Obviously, thankfully it was and I was able to get back out.” Watson explained what happened after he got to the hospital, where doctors had to rule out internal bleeding. “No internal bleeding. No anything that was raising suspicion,” Watson said when describing what the tests had revealed. “Because I was spitting a little blood at first, so they just wanted to make sure there was nothing crazy.” Watson later said he had a broken rib and compared the ordeal to watching World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) as a kid. The fifth-year pro added he was “feeling good” and expressed his appreciation to the Packers crowd for their reaction to his return. “It was surreal running out and just hearing the fans having my back like that,” Watson said. “It’s tough any time that you have to go off the field or you think you’re injured, or you’re going down with something. So, just to come back out here and get that kind of response from the fans was incredible.” With the win, the Packers improved to 5-3 on the season and will next face the New England Patriots on the road on November 8. The Panthers fell to 3-4 and will host the Denver Broncos on November 8.

articles.title: Fernando Sanz: "Renunciar al Mundial condena al Málaga a ser un equipo pequeño"
articles.standfirst: El expresidente, muy tajante con la actualidad blanquiazul
articles.summary: El expresidente, muy tajante con la actualidad blanquiazul
articles.body: Fernando Sanz ha sido el protagonista de una nueva edición de las “Charlas de Primera” organizadas por la Asociación de Periodistas Deportivos de Málaga. El que fuera jugador y presidente del Málaga CF repasó durante el encuentro sus diferentes etapas vinculadas al club y abordó también algunos de los principales asuntos que rodean actualmente a la entidad blanquiazul. Uno de los temas centrales fue el futuro de La Rosaleda. Sanz se mostró partidario de que el estadio continúe en los terrenos de Martiricos, aunque considera que Málaga dejó pasar una oportunidad importante al no disponer de un nuevo recinto con motivo del Mundial 2030. “Renunciar a la Copa del Mundo condena al Málaga CF a ser un equipo pequeño”, afirmó. También se refirió a la situación de la propiedad y a la administración judicial, cuya duración considera excesiva después de siete años. Aunque reconoce no ser jurista, aseguró estar convencido de que existen alternativas para poner fin a una situación que se ha prolongado demasiado. Durante la charla, Sanz estuvo acompañado por antiguos futbolistas como Jesús Gámez, Calatayud y De Los Santos, además del exentrenador Antonio Tapia. El exdirigente recordó con especial cariño su relación con el Málaga, un club al que atribuye un papel fundamental en su trayectoria. “Me sanó como futbolista y es un equipo y una ciudad con la que siempre estaré en deuda”, señaló. También reivindicó la gestión económica de su etapa en la presidencia. Sanz puso el foco en el cumplimiento de las obligaciones salariales y destacó que durante su mandato las nóminas se abonaron siempre “en tiempo y forma”. “Peleábamos por ahorrar cada euro por el bien del Málaga CF. Sabíamos que teníamos un tope para los jugadores a nivel de salario y de ahí no podíamos pasar”, explicó. Una política que, según recordó, provocó la salida de algunos futbolistas, pero permitió apostar por jugadores identificados con el club. Como ejemplo, señaló el equipo dirigido por Antonio Tapia que terminó octavo en Primera División. Preguntado por la posibilidad de regresar algún día al Málaga CF, Fernando Sanz dejó claro que cualquier proyecto futuro debería estar basado en un componente emocional y en un vínculo real con la entidad. También lamentó que ni los actuales propietarios ni la administración judicial hayan recurrido a él durante estos años para pedirle consejo sobre el club, aunque sí ha recibido invitaciones para acudir a partidos en el palco de La Rosaleda. El exfutbolista reconoció además cierta frustración porque su figura haya quedado más asociada a su etapa como presidente que a sus años como jugador, pese a que pasó mucho más tiempo sobre el terreno de juego que en los despachos. La situación de la familia Al-Thani también apareció durante la conversación. Sanz fue preguntado por la posición que, a su juicio, debería adoptar Abdullah Al-Thani ante la situación judicial de su hijo, Nasser. Su respuesta estuvo marcada por la perspectiva personal y familiar: “Creo que cualquiera de las personas que estamos aquí presentes que tenemos hijos, lucharíamos con todo para llegar a una solución y poder conseguir que nuestro hijo salga de la cárcel”.

articles.title: Afcon to return to two-year cycle after Caf u-turn
articles.summary: The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a review into December's decision to host it every four years instead.
articles.body:
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.

Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.

"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.

The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season.

Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July last year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates.

The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup.

The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco.

articles.title: Valdebebas tiene otra joya: el fenómeno Alberto Ruiz
articles.standfirst: Ocho goles y una final mundialista avalan la irrupción del zurdo del Madrid, que lleva años creciendo en La Fábrica a pasos agigantados
articles.summary: Ocho goles y una final mundialista avalan la irrupción del zurdo del Madrid, que lleva años creciendo en La Fábrica a pasos agigantados
articles.body: Alberto Ruiz es uno de los nombres propios del fútbol español en el Mundial sub-15 que se disputa en Bakú. El joven talento del Real Madrid está siendo una de las grandes sensaciones del torneo, en el que España se ha clasificado para la final frente a la República Checa (DAZN, 15h). Con el dorsal 10 a la espalda, el futbolista manchego ha firmado actuaciones decisivas y llega a la cita por el título como uno de los máximos goleadores de la competición, con ocho tantos. Nacido en La Solana (Ciudad Real) el 9 de febrero de 2011 (15 años), Alberto Ruiz llegó a la cantera del Real Madrid en 2019, cuando apenas tenía ocho años. Se incorporó al Benjamín B después de llamar la atención de los técnicos madridistas. Un hat-trick en un partido entre el equipo de su localidad y el conjunto blanco resultó determinante para que se incorporase a La Fábrica. Sus primeros pasos en Valdebebas fueron compatibles con su vida en La Solana: durante un tiempo entrenaba dos días en Madrid y el resto de la semana en su pueblo. Posteriormente, su familia se trasladó a la capital para acompañarle en su desarrollo futbolístico. Desde entonces, Alberto ha ido superando etapas dentro de la cantera madridista. Benjamín, Alevín, Infantil y Cadete han sido los escalones de un recorrido que le ha llevado hasta el Cadete A, categoría en la que milita actualmente. Su progresión, que no ha pasado inadvertida en Valdebebas, es de las que obliga a fijar como uno de los elegidos. La temporada pasada, todavía en edad infantil, firmó unos registros extraordinarios: 34 goles y 19 asistencias con el Infantil A. Unas cifras que explican buena parte de las expectativas que ha generado a su alrededor. Cada vez que sale de casa, su talento siempre ha encontrado la manera de sorprender a todos. Como en 2023, cuando fue se llevó el MVP y máximo goleador de LaLiga Promises 2023, con nueve tantos. Por eso, en la cantera blanca lleva tiempo siendo uno de los futbolistas a seguir y su crecimiento le ha permitido hacerse un hueco en las categorías inferiores de la selección española. Con España ha encontrado otro escenario para demostrar sus condiciones. Zurdo y capacidad para desenvolverse como mediapunta o extremo derecho, es un futbolista que destaca por su golpeo, su facilidad para conducir hacia dentro y su habilidad para encontrar posiciones de remate. En el Real Madrid suele partir desde posiciones ofensivas, buscando diagonales desde la derecha para aprovechar su pierna izquierda, aunque también tiene recursos para participar en la elaboración y encontrar el último pase. Su evolución va más allá de los números. Ha ido creciendo en el apartado físico, en la toma de decisiones y en su capacidad para marcar diferencias. Es un jugador con personalidad, visión de juego y facilidad para generar peligro desde la frontal. También ha demostrado una faceta menos visible, pero importante para su desarrollo: su compromiso colectivo. En este Mundial, por ejemplo, ha llegado a desempeñarse incluso como lateral izquierdo cuando el equipo lo ha necesitado. En Bakú está viviendo, en cualquier caso, uno de los grandes escaparates de su todavía corta trayectoria. Alberto ha sido decisivo para que España alcance la final. Marcó en la fase de grupos y protagonizó actuaciones especialmente destacadas en las eliminatorias, con dos goles ante Colombia en los cuartos de final y otros dos en las semifinales frente a Grecia. Ahora le espera la República Checa, último obstáculo para conquistar el título mundial.
