articles.title: ‘The grass isn’t always greener’: Troy Aikman reportedly sent a message on ESPN after leaving Fox
articles.summary: Troy Aikman left Fox for ESPN in 2022 in a move that made him one of the highest-paid broadcasters in sports. But with his relationship with Joe Buck falling...
articles.body:
Troy Aikman left Fox for ESPN in 2022 in a move that made him one of the highest-paid broadcasters in sports. But with his relationship with Joe Buck falling apart and no new contract in sight, it sounds like Aikman may have some regrets.

According to a new report, Aikman made a surprise appearance at a retirement party for his former coach, Jimmy Johnson, hosted by Fox in 2025, where he offered some telling words to his old colleagues. The report also details the ugly argument between Aikman and Buck before a Monday Night Football broadcast earlier this month.

Aikman and Buck called six Super Bowls together at Fox before ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro lured them to Monday Night Football in 2022. Aikman signed a five-year, $90 million deal, while Buck got $75 million, with both contracts set to culminate with ESPN's first Super Bowl broadcast in February.

But ESPN has since given Buck a six-year, $108 million extension, while Aikman hasn't received an offer. Aikman has said that he'll be a free agent after the season, and the tension between the two boiled over in the booth before the Bills-Rams game on Oct. 12, according to Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel .

One source even claimed that the argument nearly got physical . The NFL insisted it had "no concern" about the pair, pointing to their broadcasts as proof that they're still on the same page.

The two have continued to call games together without any visible friction. But according to Puck's Dylan Byers, it's still "not a tension-free zone" behind the scenes, and Aikman appears unlikely to return to ESPN after the season.

In a deep dive on the falling out, Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reported that Fox invited Aikman to make a surprise appearance at Johnson's retirement party in the summer of 2025, despite the fact that Aikman had left the network on bad terms.

Aikman received a standing ovation and got a little emotional, offering some kind words about his old network before adding a telling line, according to three sources present.

"In case anyone is wondering, the grass isn't always greener," Aikman said, per The Athletic .

Clearly, Aikman's time at ESPN appears to be winding down, and he isn't pretending the move worked out the way he hoped.

articles.title: Dover boys soccer wins back-to-back district titles over New Phila
articles.summary: Owen Duda came through again for Dover, scoring the decisive goal in a shutout of New Philadelphia to claim consecutive district titles.
articles.body:
For the second consecutive season, the Dover boys soccer team found itself celebrating a district championship at the expense of its biggest rival.

Behind an early goal from senior Owen Duda and a strong defensive performance, the Crimson Tornadoes defeated New Philadelphia 1-0 on Thursday, Oct. 29, to capture their second straight district championship, securing another trip to the OHSAA regional tournament.

This time, the senior found the back of the net early, giving the Crimson Tornadoes a lead they would protect for the remainder of the game.

After his performance against John Glenn, Duda said he entered Thursday's championship with a renewed sense of confidence.

"I can do this. I have the confidence to do it," he said. "I can put it in the back of the net, and I can lead my team."

Knowing the importance of the rivalry matchup, Duda also made it a priority to ensure his teammates were energized from the moment they arrived.

"I made sure that the entire time we're warming up, the entire bus right here was loud," he said. "During warmups, we're here yelling while we're shooting.

"You have to get the positive energy going early."

With the early advantage, Dover coach Austin Wade faced a decision about how aggressively his team should continue to attack.

Rather than completely shifting into a defensive approach, Wade wanted his players to maintain the possession and offensive opportunities that established the lead.

"We talk about wanting to sit in and get a little more defensive, but at the same time, we don't want to change from our gameplan," Wade said. "We felt like we were able to get good looks and good control, especially in the midfield and up top, and we didn't want to give in to that."

Wade said managing his players' stamina and making adjustments were important factors in protecting the one-goal advantage. For Wade, the opportunity to celebrate another district championship with his eight seniors made the victory particularly meaningful.

"It doesn't get old," Wade said. "These seniors have given everything to this program."

Wade credited the leadership of his upperclassmen for helping the Crimson Tornadoes navigate the pressure of another postseason rivalry showdown.

"They're just the backbone for the rest of the team," he said. "They lead by example, and they are true role models for these younger guys."

The significance of winning another championship against New Philadelphia was not lost on Wade.

"There's a certain respect for this level of rivalry, and it just makes the game so exciting," he said. "I'm really grateful to be with these kids and with these coaches, and come here and have this type of rivalry game with these high stakes."

For Duda, the championship was about more than defeating a rival or adding another trophy to the program's collection.

"It's the first time in a long time that we've actually won two in a row," Duda said. "This is probably by far my favorite group of guys. And I'm just glad I get to celebrate it with them."

Now, Dover turns its attention toward unfinished business.

Last season, the Crimson Tornadoes advanced to the regional championship before falling short of a trip to the state semifinals.

Duda said last year's postseason matchups against Jackson and Bishop Watterson taught him what to expect as the competition gets tougher.

"The opponents get bigger and stronger," he said. "We just have to keep up."

Wade echoed that sentiment, emphasizing that each postseason presents different challenges and requires adjustments.

"It's a different level for sure, and so tactics change a little bit from team to team," he said. "These guys, they'll be ready tomorrow, looking to learn and get better.

"They're excited about the opportunity."

articles.summary: La UEFA no termina de dar con la persona que se presente a las elecciones de la FIFA y el nombre del francés sigue en la agenda
articles.body: La FIFA tendrá el próximo 18 de marzo nuevo presidente con Gianni Infantino ahora mismo como único candidato para la reelección. El tiempo se agota, hasta el 18 de noviembre hay plazo para anunciar candidatura, pero el frente anti Infantino, que en el sorteo de la Champions en Mónaco confirmó que buscarían una alternativa en colaboración con la Concacaf, (las dos confederaciones que han puesto toda la carne en el asador para relevar al actual presidente tras su intento fallido de privatizar el Mundial) pero aún hoy siguen en la búsqueda. El nombre de Arsène Wenger lleva tiempo en las quinielas, pero lo que parecía una opción remota cobra cada vez más fuerza según ha podido saber MARCA. La primera opción que barajaba la UEFA es que fuera un candidato no europeo y el preferido era Victor Montagliani, al frente de la Concacaf, pero esta opción ha ido perdiendo peso. El diario L'Équipe ha destapado tres pistas próximas al presidente de la UEFA, Aleksander Ceferin. Uno es el presidente de la Federación de Hungría, Sandor Csanyi y vicepresidente del Consejo de la FIFA. Es un multimillonario y magnate húngaro que podría además afrontar la financiación de la campaña. El otro es Razvan Burleanu, presidente de la Federación de Rumanía, que aspiraba a relevar al propio Ceferin hasta que ha anunciado que se presenta en abril a un nuevo mandato, y el ex presidente de la Federación portuguesa Fernando Gomes. No hay aún decisión tomada al respecto y la UEFA solo apunta que siguen en la búsqueda ya que se lleva todo este asunto con total discreción. La opción de Wenger, que no ha tomado una decisión, implica dejar patente sus discrepancias con Infantino que quedaron patentes tras la polémica maniobra del máximo mandatario del fútbol mundial. Como director de Desarrollo Mundial del Fútbol de la FIFA, el ex entrenador del Arsenal quiso dejar claro en su momento que tampoco estaba al corriente de esta maniobra y mostró su desacuerdo a la iniciativa. Wenger acaba de sufrir además otro revés ya que está a punto de caer en saco roto su regla del fuera de juego, conocida como ley Wenger, al ser descartada según la Ser por los dirigentes de la IFAB en su última reunión. El principal cambio se basaba en la posición del atacante para determinar si había fuera de juego y había sido probada en la Liga canadiense. El jugador sólo iba a estar en posición incorrecta si todo el cuerpo estaba adelantado. Desde algunos sectores del fútbol europeo se ha animado a Wenger para que dé el paso porque se le ve como una figura muy respetada y de consenso, pero el ex entrenador, inmerso ahora en el Mundial sub 15, se la ha visto muy comprometido con este nuevo formato de Copa del Mundo que termina hoy Azerbaiyán y muchos dudan de que dé al final un paso tan brusco contra el actual presidente de la FIFA.
